EX-001.title: EX-001 — Bookworm
EX-001.body_html: A moth ate words. When I heard of that wonder, it seemed to me a strange thing—that the worm should swallow the riddle of certain men, a thief in the darkness, and their glorious pronouncements.
characteristics: Accepted Variants: [bookworm, book worm, moth, book-moth, worm, insect]
Clue: This creature loves knowledge more than you do—it consumes words.
EX-001.source: Anglo-Saxon Riddles of the Exeter Book/Annotated/42 - Wikisource; The riddles of the Exeter book - Internet Archive
EX-001.licence: Public domain; translation by Paull Franklin Baum (1963)

EX-002.title: EX-002 — Key
EX-002.lead: I am a most strange creature, for I satisfy women, a single thing by nature.
EX-002.body_html: I am a most strange creature, for I satisfy women, a single thing by nature. No harm do I inflict on the creatures of this estate if the man who inhabits the stronghold wishes to use me rightly.
characteristics: Clue: You use me to grant access to what is kept hidden.
EX-002.source: Anglo-Saxon Riddles of the Exeter Book - Wikisource
EX-002.licence: Public domain; Exeter Book (original manuscript c. 10th century)

EX-003.title: EX-003 — Plow
EX-003.lead: I stand with my feet in the earth, a warrior with twisted limbs.
EX-003.body_html: I stand with my feet in the earth, a warrior with twisted limbs. I am strong, I wage fierce war.
characteristics: Clue: I break ground to feed the people.
EX-003.source: Anglo-Saxon Riddles of the Exeter Book - Wikisource

EX-004.title: EX-004 — Dog
EX-004.lead: I am silent when I walk, when I eat, when I drink; but when I sleep I roar fearfully.
EX-004.body_html: I am silent when I walk, when I eat, when I drink; but when I sleep I roar fearfully.
characteristics: Clue: A loyal companion that barks in dreams.
EX-004.source: Anglo-Saxon Riddles of the Exeter Book/Index of Solutions - Wikisource

EX-005.title: EX-005 — Fire
EX-005.lead: Boneless it dwells in bosom, boneless flows out; hard in head, soft in breast, it gives glory to noble kinsmen and comfort to the common folk.
EX-005.body_html: Boneless it dwells in bosom, boneless flows out; hard in head, soft in breast, it gives glory to noble kinsmen and comfort to the common folk.
characteristics: Clue: I consume but leave ash; I warm but can burn.
EX-005.source: Anglo-Saxon Riddles of the Exeter Book - Wikisource

EX-006.title: EX-006 — Sword
EX-006.lead: I am a precious thing, wrapped in skin, adorned with hair.
EX-006.body_html: I am a precious thing, wrapped in skin, adorned with hair. I am the delight of warriors, ornament of nobles.
characteristics: Clue: I hang at a warrior's side, both decoration and death-dealer.
EX-006.source: Anglo-Saxon Riddles of the Exeter Book - Wikisource

EX-007.title: EX-007 — Ship
EX-007.lead: I travel over the mountains and through vales, through groves and along glens.
EX-007.body_html: I travel over the mountains and through vales, through groves and along glens. I am carried in hand and brought to hall; I lodge in the breast.
characteristics: Accepted Variants: [ship, boat, vessel, sailing vessel]
Clue: I sail the seas but also dwell in hearts.
EX-007.source: Anglo-Saxon Riddles of the Exeter Book - Wikisource

EX-008.title: EX-008 — Water
EX-008.lead: I am bound yet have no chains.
EX-008.body_html: I am bound yet have no chains. I move the whole year yet never grow weary. Bright is my home, and I am a creature that dreads evil men.
characteristics: Accepted Variants: [water, ice, river, stream, wave]
Clue: I can be solid or liquid, and all life depends on me.

GR-001.title: GR-001 — Human being
GR-001.lead: What creature goes on four feet in the morning, two feet at noon, and three feet in the evening?
GR-001.body_html: What creature goes on four feet in the morning, two feet at noon, and three feet in the evening?
characteristics: Accepted Variants: [human, man, person, mankind, human being]
Clue: This being changes its form throughout a lifetime.
Tradition/Origin: The Riddle of the Sphinx (Greek mythology), posed to Oedipus
GR-001.source: Riddle of the Sphinx - Quatr.us Study Guides; The Sphinx – Mythology Unbound

NO-001.title: NO-001 — Skinfaxi
NO-001.lead: What is the name of the horse that draws the chariot of day across the sky?
NO-001.body_html: What is the name of the horse that draws the chariot of day across the sky?
characteristics: Clue: His mane illuminates the night sky.
Tradition/Origin: Norse Mythology, Vafthrudnismal (wisdom contest of Odin and Vafthrudnir)
NO-001.source: The Poetic Edda: Vafthruthnismol - Internet Sacred Text Archive

NO-002.title: NO-002 — Saevingul
NO-002.lead: What is the name of the horse that the giant Hrym rode when the bonds are broken?
NO-002.body_html: What is the name of the horse that the giant Hrym rode when the bonds are broken?
characteristics: Clue: A steed that rides at the end of all things.
NO-002.source: The Poetic Edda: Vafthruthnismol - Internet Sacred Text Archive

EN-001.title: EN-001 — Candle
EN-001.lead: Little Nancy Etticote, in a white petticoat, with a red nose; the longer she stands, the shorter she grows.
EN-001.body_html: Little Nancy Etticote, in a white petticoat, with a red nose; the longer she stands, the shorter she grows.
characteristics: Accepted Variants: [candle, taper, light, wax candle]
Clue: I burn away as I illuminate.
Tradition/Origin: English nursery rhyme / Mother Goose
EN-001.source: Mother Goose's Nursery Rhymes - Project Gutenberg

EN-002.title: EN-002 — Egg
EN-002.lead: In marble halls as white as milk, lined with a skin as soft as silk; within a fountain crystal-clear, a golden apple doth appear.
EN-002.body_html: In marble halls as white as milk, lined with a skin as soft as silk; within a fountain crystal-clear, a golden apple doth appear. No doors there are to this stronghold, yet thieves break in and steal the gold.
characteristics: Accepted Variants: [egg, chicken egg, goose egg]
Clue: Layers of protection hide the treasure inside.
EN-002.source: In Marble Walls As White As Milk - Mama Lisa's World
EN-002.licence: Public domain (collected in Leslie Brooke's 1916 nursery rhyme collection)

EN-003.title: EN-003 — A man sitting on a stool with a leg of mutton; a dog steals it
EN-003.lead: Two legs sat upon three legs, with one leg in his lap; in comes four legs, and runs away with one leg.
EN-003.body_html: Two legs sat upon three legs, with one leg in his lap; in comes four legs, and runs away with one leg. Up jumps two legs, catches up three legs, throws it after four legs, and makes him bring one leg back.
characteristics: Answer: A man sitting on a stool with a leg of mutton; a dog steals it
Accepted Variants: [man and dog, stool and meat, human and dog]
Clue: A feast interrupted by a thief with four paws.
Tradition/Origin: English nursery rhyme / Mother Goose
EN-003.source: Mother Goose's Nursery Rhymes - Project Gutenberg

EN-004.title: EN-004 — A bird's eye
EN-004.lead: I have a little sister; they call her Peep, Peep.
EN-004.body_html: I have a little sister; they call her Peep, Peep. She wades the water, deep, deep, deep; she climbs the mountains, high, high, high. Poor little thing! she has but one eye.
characteristics: Answer: A bird's eye (or potato eye, or spring of water)
Accepted Variants: [eye, bird eye, potato eye, water spring]
Clue: It sees the world but cannot look both ways.
Tradition/Origin: English nursery rhyme / Mother Goose
EN-004.source: Mother Goose's Nursery Rhymes - Project Gutenberg

EN-005.title: EN-005 — Needle and thread
EN-005.lead: Old Mother Twitchett had one eye, and a long tail which she let fly, and every time she went over a gap, she left a bit of her tail in a trap.
EN-005.body_html: Old Mother Twitchett had one eye, and a long tail which she let fly, and every time she went over a gap, she left a bit of her tail in a trap.
characteristics: Accepted Variants: [needle, needle and thread, sewing needle]
Clue: I pierce cloth and leave my trace behind.
Tradition/Origin: English nursery rhyme / Mother Goose

EN-006.title: EN-006 — Candle snuffer
EN-006.lead: Peter White will ne'er go right; would you know the reason why?
EN-006.body_html: Peter White will ne'er go right; would you know the reason why? He follows his nose wherever he goes, and that stands all awry.
characteristics: Answer: Candle snuffer (or similar crooked tool)
Clue: A crooked helper that serves by following its bent nature.
Tradition/Origin: English nursery rhyme / Mother Goose
EN-006.source: Mother Goose's Nursery Rhymes - Project Gutenberg

EN-007.title: EN-007 — Egg
EN-007.lead: As white as milk, as black as coal, as soft as silk, with a heart of gold.
EN-007.body_html: As white as milk, as black as coal, as soft as silk, with a heart of gold.
characteristics: Clue: A simple treasure found in nature, white and dark together.
Tradition/Origin: English nursery rhyme / folk riddle
EN-007.source: Mother Goose nursery rhymes - Internet Archive

JW-001.title: JW-001 — Honey
JW-001.lead: Out of the eater came something to eat, and out of the strong came something sweet.
JW-001.body_html: Out of the eater came something to eat, and out of the strong came something sweet.
characteristics: Clue: A bee's home grew inside a predator.
Tradition/Origin: Samson's Riddle, Bible (Judges 14:14), public domain

JW-002.title: JW-002 — Seven days of menstruation; nine months of pregnancy; two breasts; one child
JW-002.lead: Seven issue and nine enter; two yield draught, one drinks.
JW-002.body_html: Seven issue and nine enter; two yield draught, one drinks.
characteristics: Answer: Seven days of menstruation; nine months of pregnancy; two breasts; one child
Clue: A woman's passage through motherhood.
Tradition/Origin: Solomon's Riddle from Rabbinic Literature
JW-002.source: The Riddles of Solomon in Rabbinic Literature - Wikisource

JW-003.title: JW-003 — The womb
characteristics: Clue: A fortress of flesh that contains new life.
Tradition/Origin: Solomon's Riddle from Rabbinic Literature
JW-003.source: The Riddles of Solomon in Rabbinic Literature - Wikisource

JW-004.title: JW-004 — A ship
JW-004.lead: Living moves not; head cut off, moves.
JW-004.body_html: Living moves not; head cut off, moves.
characteristics: Clue: Once alive as a tree, now silent wood that travels.
Tradition/Origin: Solomon's Riddle from Rabbinic Literature
JW-004.source: The Riddles of Solomon in Rabbinic Literature - Wikisource

JW-005.title: JW-005 — Jonah
JW-005.lead: Dead lived, grave moves, dead prays.
characteristics: Clue: A man swallowed by the sea yet called upon his God.
Tradition/Origin: Solomon's Riddle from Rabbinic Literature (biblical allusion)
JW-005.source: The Riddles of Solomon in Rabbinic Literature - Wikisource

CH-001.title: CH-001 — Silkworm
CH-001.lead: This lovely maiden eats no meat but eats leaves.
CH-001.body_html: This lovely maiden eats no meat but eats leaves. She labours each day spinning and weaving for the benefit of others.
characteristics: Accepted Variants: [silkworm, silk worm, worm, insect]
Clue: A humble spinner that works itself to death for silk.
CH-001.source: 8 Lantern Riddles to Celebrate the Chinese Lantern Festival - The Epoch Times

CH-002.title: CH-002 — A lock
CH-002.lead: He devotes his life to looking after the house.
CH-002.body_html: He devotes his life to looking after the house. His mate always follows when the master goes out.
characteristics: Accepted Variants: [lock, padlock, key lock, security lock]
Clue: Metal teeth hold secrets shut.
CH-002.source: 8 Lantern Riddles to Celebrate the Chinese Lantern Festival - The Epoch Times

CH-003.title: CH-003 — The moon
CH-003.lead: It's been around for millions of years, but it's no more than a month old.
CH-003.body_html: It's been around for millions of years, but it's no more than a month old.
characteristics: Clue: Ancient in the sky, forever renewing itself.
CH-003.source: 8 Lantern Riddles to Celebrate the Chinese Lantern Festival - The Epoch Times

CH-004.title: CH-004 — Your name
CH-004.lead: What belongs to you but others use it more than you do?
CH-004.body_html: What belongs to you but others use it more than you do?
characteristics: Clue: Others speak it more often than you hear it.
CH-004.source: 8 Lantern Riddles to Celebrate the Chinese Lantern Festival - The Epoch Times

CH-005.title: CH-005 — A clock
CH-005.lead: It works hard all its life, counting numbers day and night, but never gets past 12.
CH-005.body_html: It works hard all its life, counting numbers day and night, but never gets past 12.
characteristics: Clue: It measures time by numbers that repeat.
CH-005.source: 8 Lantern Riddles to Celebrate the Chinese Lantern Festival - The Epoch Times

CH-006.title: CH-006 — Chopsticks
CH-006.lead: They look like twin brothers, both sturdy and tall.
CH-006.body_html: They look like twin brothers, both sturdy and tall. They work together and go everywhere together.
characteristics: Clue: A pair of helpers that deliver food to your mouth.
CH-006.source: 8 Lantern Riddles to Celebrate the Chinese Lantern Festival - The Epoch Times

CH-007.title: CH-007 — Your shadow
CH-007.lead: I can follow you for thousands of miles and not miss home.
CH-007.body_html: I can follow you for thousands of miles and not miss home. I do not fear cold or fire.
characteristics: Clue: It leaves when the light does, but never truly leaves you.
CH-007.source: 8 Lantern Riddles to Celebrate the Chinese Lantern Festival - The Epoch Times

AF-001.title: AF-001 — Egg
AF-001.lead: My house has no doors or windows; yet there are living things within.
AF-001.body_html: My house has no doors or windows; yet there are living things within.
characteristics: Accepted Variants: [egg, coconut, nut, seed, enclosed space]
Clue: Break me open and find life waiting.
AF-001.source: African Proverbs and Riddles - Internet Archive

AF-002.title: AF-002 — A coin
AF-002.lead: I have a head and a tail but no body.
AF-002.body_html: I have a head and a tail but no body.
characteristics: Clue: Two sides, no life, yet humans treasure me.
AF-002.source: African Proverbs and Riddles - Internet Archive
AF-002.licence: Public domain (traditional folklore, compiled by Laura Gibbs)

AF-003.title: AF-003 — A fish trap
AF-003.lead: What looks like a house but has many windows?
AF-003.body_html: What looks like a house but has many windows?
characteristics: Answer: A fish trap (or honeycomb, or sieve)
Accepted Variants: [fish trap, honeycomb, sieve, trap, net]
Clue: It catches what swims or flows through it.
AF-003.source: African Proverbs and Riddles - Internet Archive

AF-004.title: AF-004 — A postage stamp
AF-004.lead: I travel all around the world but never leave my corner.
AF-004.body_html: I travel all around the world but never leave my corner.
characteristics: Clue: I stick to messages and journey across continents.
AF-004.source: African Proverbs and Riddles - Internet Archive
AF-004.licence: Public domain (collected in modern African riddle traditions)

FO-001.title: FO-001 — Footsteps
FO-001.lead: The more you take, the more you leave behind.
FO-001.body_html: The more you take, the more you leave behind. What am I?
characteristics: Accepted Variants: [footsteps, steps, tracks, footprints, trails]
Clue: I mark where you have been.
Tradition/Origin: Universal folk riddle (widespread in many traditions)

FO-002.title: FO-002 — A cow
FO-002.lead: Four hang, two point the way, two are useful, one sits in judgment, and the rest do the work.
FO-002.body_html: Four hang, two point the way, two are useful, one sits in judgment, and the rest do the work.
characteristics: Clue: A common farm animal whose parts serve many purposes.
Tradition/Origin: Universal folk riddle (widespread across Indo-European traditions)
FO-002.source: Four Hang; Two Point the Way - Wikipedia

FO-003.title: FO-003 — A clock
FO-003.lead: I have a face and two hands, but no arms and no legs.
FO-003.body_html: I have a face and two hands, but no arms and no legs.
characteristics: Accepted Variants: [clock, watch, face, dial, timepiece]
Clue: I measure the passing of each day.

FO-004.title: FO-004 — An echo
FO-004.lead: I speak without a mouth and hear without ears.
FO-004.body_html: I speak without a mouth and hear without ears. I have no body, but I come alive with wind. What am I?
characteristics: Clue: I repeat your words but live in emptiness.

FO-005.title: FO-005 — A postage stamp
FO-005.lead: I can travel around the world while staying in a corner.
FO-005.body_html: I can travel around the world while staying in a corner.
characteristics: Clue: Glued to paper, I go everywhere letters go.

FO-006.title: FO-006 — Nothing
FO-006.body_html: The rich need me. The poor have me. If you eat me, you will die. What am I?
characteristics: Clue: The wealthy cannot afford to lack it; the poor have only this.

FO-007.title: FO-007 — The letter "R
FO-007.lead: What is seen in the middle of March and April that cannot be seen at any other time of year?
FO-007.body_html: What is seen in the middle of March and April that cannot be seen at any other time of year?
characteristics: Clue: Look at the spelling of the months.

FO-008.title: FO-008 — A river
FO-008.lead: What has a bed but never sleeps, has a bank but no money, and has a mouth but never speaks?
FO-008.body_html: What has a bed but never sleeps, has a bank but no money, and has a mouth but never speaks?

FO-009.title: FO-009 — Your breath
FO-009.lead: What is harder to catch the faster you run?
FO-009.body_html: What is harder to catch the faster you run?
characteristics: Clue: The more you exert yourself, the more elusive it becomes.

FO-010.title: FO-010 — A joke
FO-010.lead: What can be cracked, made, told, and played?
FO-010.body_html: What can be cracked, made, told, and played?
characteristics: Clue: It brings laughter when delivered well.

FO-011.title: FO-011 — An artichoke
FO-011.lead: What has a heart that does not beat?
FO-011.body_html: What has a heart that does not beat?
characteristics: Clue: A thorny plant with a tender center.

FO-012.title: FO-012 — A human being
FO-012.lead: What walks on four legs in the morning, two legs at noon, and three legs in the evening?
FO-012.body_html: What walks on four legs in the morning, two legs at noon, and three legs in the evening?
characteristics: Answer: A human being (at different life stages; variant of Sphinx riddle)
Clue: This is life's journey measured in feet.
Tradition/Origin: Universal folk riddle (variant of Sphinx riddle)

FO-013.title: FO-013 — Pencil lead
FO-013.lead: I am taken from a mine and shut up in a wooden case, from which I am never released.
FO-013.body_html: I am taken from a mine and shut up in a wooden case, from which I am never released. What am I?
characteristics: Accepted Variants: [pencil lead, graphite, lead, writing material]
Clue: I write the world but am imprisoned in wood.

FO-014.title: FO-014 — The letter "M
FO-014.lead: What comes once in a minute, twice in a moment, and never in one thousand years?
FO-014.body_html: What comes once in a minute, twice in a moment, and never in one thousand years?

FO-015.title: FO-015 — A mountain
FO-015.lead: What has roots that nobody sees, is taller than trees, up, up it goes, and yet it never grows?
FO-015.body_html: What has roots that nobody sees, is taller than trees, up, up it goes, and yet it never grows?
characteristics: Clue: Ancient stone that reaches the sky.

FO-016.title: FO-016 — Charcoal
FO-016.lead: What is black when you buy it, red when you use it, and gray when you throw it away?
FO-016.body_html: What is black when you buy it, red when you use it, and gray when you throw it away?
characteristics: Clue: I fuel fires but am destroyed by them.

FO-017.title: FO-017 — Are you asleep?
FO-017.lead: What question can you never answer "yes" to?
FO-017.body_html: What question can you never answer "yes" to?
characteristics: Accepted Variants: [are you asleep, sleeping question]
Clue: Answer it and you contradict yourself.

FO-018.title: FO-018 — Light
FO-018.lead: What can fill a room but takes up no space?
FO-018.body_html: What can fill a room but takes up no space?
characteristics: Clue: It comes from sun, lamp, or fire.

FO-019.title: FO-019 — Fire
FO-019.lead: I am not alive, but I grow.
FO-019.body_html: I am not alive, but I grow. I don't have lungs, but I need air. I don't have a mouth, but water kills me. What am I?
characteristics: Clue: I am born of heat and feed on fuel.

FO-020.title: FO-020 — An echo
FO-020.lead: I speak all languages and have visited every country in the world.
FO-020.body_html: I speak all languages and have visited every country in the world. What am I?
characteristics: Clue: I repeat what you say in any tongue.

FO-021.title: FO-021 — A cloud
FO-021.lead: What is white and fluffy, and when you touch it, it rains?
FO-021.body_html: What is white and fluffy, and when you touch it, it rains?
characteristics: Clue: I float in the sky and bring water to earth.

FO-022.title: FO-022 — Tomorrow
FO-022.lead: I am always coming but never arrive.
FO-022.body_html: I am always coming but never arrive. What am I?
characteristics: Clue: It is always promised but never truly comes.

FO-023.title: FO-023 — (This is a trick question; the answer is "I don't know" or depends on context)
FO-023.lead: What is the difference between a apple and an orange?
FO-023.body_html: What is the difference between a apple and an orange?
characteristics: Answer: (This is a trick question; the answer is "I don't know" or depends on context)
Accepted Variants: [color, skin, taste, texture, fruit]
Clue: This may not have a single answer.

FO-024.title: FO-024 — A bottle
FO-024.lead: I have a neck but no head.
FO-024.body_html: I have a neck but no head. What am I?
characteristics: Clue: I hold liquids but cannot drink them.

FO-025.title: FO-025 — Short
FO-025.lead: What word becomes shorter when you add two letters to it?
FO-025.body_html: What word becomes shorter when you add two letters to it?
characteristics: Clue: Add "er" to make it short-er.

FO-026.title: FO-026 — The horizon
FO-026.lead: What is the one thing that all wise men, regardless of their politics or religion, agree is between heaven and earth?
FO-026.body_html: What is the one thing that all wise men, regardless of their politics or religion, agree is between heaven and earth?
characteristics: Clue: It divides what we see above from what we see below.

FO-027.title: FO-027 — Silence
FO-027.lead: What is so fragile that saying its name breaks it?
FO-027.body_html: What is so fragile that saying its name breaks it?
characteristics: Clue: It ends the moment you speak.
